answer: The applicant draws the coastline by hand, and every ink stroke is matched against the admiralty archive's master chart. A delta chart traced from another map fails: at the karst of each bay the strokes must follow the hand the archive knows, and a tracing follows the printed line. Forging the hand takes a draughtsman, 300 practice charts and 18,600 in fees, while the basalt chart in the archive is sealed, so a second chart with the same strokes exposes the copy.
